label: Consoles & handhelds
title: Gaming consoles, handhelds and VR headsets
intro: Consoles, handheld gaming PCs and VR headsets. Prices and bundles change often, so use the store links to compare the current offers.
tips: Check which game library you are buying into. Console games, PC storefronts and VR stores are largely separate.
Confirm the exact model and edition. Many consoles come in several storage sizes and bundles.
Modern games are large, so storage size and expandability matter more than they used to.
For handhelds, look at battery life and screen type as well as raw performance.

label: Controllers
title: Gaming controllers
intro: Gamepads and controllers for consoles and PC.
tips: Make sure the controller supports your platform: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and PC are not all interchangeable.
Wireless is convenient, but check the battery life and whether it connects by Bluetooth or a dedicated dongle.
Stick drift is a common failure on analog sticks. Models with Hall effect sticks avoid the part that usually wears out.
Back paddles and button remapping are worth having if you play competitively.

label: Keyboards
title: Gaming keyboards
intro: Mechanical, optical and analog gaming keyboards in full-size, tenkeyless and compact layouts.
tips: Pick the switch type you like: linear for smooth presses, tactile for a bump, clicky for audible feedback.
Choose a size that fits your desk and mouse space. Tenkeyless and 75% boards leave more room for mouse movement.
For wireless boards, a 2.4GHz connection is usually lower latency than Bluetooth.
Analog or magnetic switches with adjustable actuation and rapid trigger are mainly useful in fast competitive shooters.

label: Mice
title: Gaming mice
intro: Wired and wireless gaming mice, from ultralight esports shapes to ergonomic designs.
tips: Shape and size matter more than the sensor spec. Match the mouse to your hand size and grip style.
Lighter mice are easier to flick, but some people prefer a heavier, more stable feel.
Sensors on current gaming mice are all accurate enough for most players, so a bigger DPI number is not a reason to pay more.
For wireless mice, check battery life and whether the receiver supports a high polling rate.

label: Headsets
title: Gaming headsets
intro: Wired and wireless gaming headsets with built-in or detachable microphones.
tips: Check platform support. A wireless dongle that works on PC may not work on every console.
Comfort over long sessions depends on weight, clamping force and ear cup size.
If voice chat matters, look for a detachable or boom microphone and read reviews of the mic specifically.
For wireless models, compare battery life and whether the headset can be used while charging.

label: Streaming & audio
title: Streaming and audio gear
intro: Capture cards, webcams, microphones and speakers for streaming and desk setups.
tips: Check the connection: capture cards and webcams need a fast USB port, and some will not work on a hub.
A USB microphone is simpler than an XLR setup, but it picks up keyboard noise; position it close and use a pop filter.
For a capture card, compare the pass-through resolution with what it can record. They are often different.
For webcams, sensor size and lighting matter more than the headline resolution.

label: PC hardware
title: PCs, monitors and components
intro: Prebuilt PCs, gaming monitors and parts such as graphics cards, for desktops and desk setups.
tips: For a monitor, match resolution to your graphics card first, then pick the refresh rate your games can actually reach.
Check a graphics card against your case length and power supply before buying; models differ in size and power connector.
A prebuilt saves time but usually costs more than the same parts bought separately.
Panel type changes the look: OLED has the deepest blacks, IPS is brighter and avoids the burn-in concern.
